mutant.description: FOUR controls, and one of them changed the answer. (1) THE DOWNLOAD IS THE DEPLOYED ARTIFACT: the zip's sha256 was base64-encoded and compared with the live CodeSha256, so every hash below is a statement about running bytes rather than about a file that happens to sit somewhere. (2) THE POSITIVE CONTROL BESIDE AN ABSENT ANSWER, which CLAUDE.md requires: git ls-tree of the source dir at the recorded commit. (3) A NEGATIVE control: git show of a path that genuinely does not exist at that commit, to prove the instrument can still say no. (4) The member set was checked against the source map's own files list, so NOT_IN_SOURCE_DIR could be distinguished from a vendored dependency or a build stamp.
mutant.expected: (1) base64 digest == CodeSha256. (2) both members listed at the commit. (3) rc != 0. (4) members == the map's files list.
mutant.observed: (1) qHMjXkK1/1NhmBmkK/6Q+q+WdXMRoTOprNfTixBIxaM= both ways, identical. (2) BOTH MEMBERS LISTED -- and this is the control that caught a false negative of mine: my first pass read both members ABSENT at the recorded commit (git show rc 128) because the names came from a Windows python print and each carried a trailing CR, which git reported back as 'check_triggered_by.py?'. The control contradicted the ABSENT, I stripped the CR, and both files resolved at rc 0 with byte counts matching the deployed members exactly. (3) rc != 0, so an ABSENT from this instrument is meaningful once the argument is clean. (4) the 2 members are exactly the map's 2 files, so there is no vendored dependency or build stamp in this package and NOT_IN_SOURCE_DIR is 0 by measurement rather than by assumption.

determinism.method: Every comparison is a sha256 over bytes with NOTHING normalised -- no newline translation, no whitespace stripping, no decoding before hashing -- so a repeat read of the same artifact and the same commit must return the same digests. The three planes (deployed package, recorded commit, tree HEAD) were fetched by three independent routes: an AWS package download, git show at a pinned commit, and git show at HEAD.
determinism.observed: check_triggered_by.py reads 7e813322799f4f7a on all three planes at 1825 bytes; lambda_function.py reads ead1011f45b91912 on all three at 83888 bytes. The sizes agree with the zip's own member sizes independently of the hashes. The one non-determinism encountered was in my argument handling, not in the artifacts: a trailing CR made the same git show return rc 128 and then rc 0 for what is textually the same path, which is why the corruption oracle is to echo the argument back.
